LEFT brought the eyes back to their original positions (19-23, 39-43). So the eyes move in response to arrow keys: RIGHT → eyes converge (left eye +5, right eye -5); LEFT → eyes return to original positions. Interesting — so maybe the eyes are tracking the direction? RIGHT makes the eyes look right (i.e., both eyes shift right)? But the right eye shifted left...
Wait, maybe I should think of it this way: the eyes are looking at a point. In the default state, the eyes are at columns 19-23 and 39-43, centered on column 31. After RIGHT, the eyes are at 24-28 and 34-38, centered on column 31. The center doesn't change! The gap shrinks from 16 to 6.
Hmm, so the eyes are "squinting"? Or... the character is looking at a target, and the target is... no, that's not it.
Alternative idea: the character's face has a "mouth" (a yellow/orange gap in the middle of the head, columns 32-38, rows 13-27?). Looking at the first image: there's a yellow region in the center of the head (roughly rows 13-27, columns 32-38) — that's the mouth opening. And the eyes are below it.
Hmm, wait, actually. Maybe the whole black shape is the character's body, and the yellow/orange in the middle is the mouth. When you press RIGHT, the eyes move toward the mouth? That doesn't make sense either.
Let me think from a different angle. Maybe this is a game where you move the eyes to a target, and the eyes can only move within the head. The eyes moved 5 columns in one press. Maybe each press moves the eyes 5 columns in the pressed direction, but each eye is clamped within its own "eye socket" region? The left eye moved from 19-23 to 24-28 (rightward). The right eye moved from 39-43 to 34-38 (leftward). If the right eye were also supposed to move right, it would go to 44-48, but instead it moved left...
Unless the two eyes are a single "gaze" object: the gaze center stays at 31, and the eyes... no, that's not it.
Wait, maybe I should reconsider: perhaps the eyes are looking at the mouse cursor position, and the arrow keys move a hidden cursor. Pressing RIGHT moves the cursor right, and the eyes look toward the cursor... but both eyes moved toward the center, meaning the cursor is at the center?
Or, the eyes might be tracking a target that's at the center of the board (column 31.5, row 31.5?). In the default state, the eyes are at 19-23 and 39-43 — the centers are 21 and 41, symmetric about 31. After RIGHT: 26 and 36, symmetric about 31. So the eyes are always symmetric about column 31. The gap changed from 20 (center-to-center distance 20) to 10.
Hmm, maybe the eyes are "looking" in a direction, and the direction determines the offset of each eye from the center: looking left → eyes shift left (centers 21, 41 → both -10?). Looking right → shift right? But the right eye went left.
Okay, another thought: maybe the character's head is rotating around the center (31, 31). The head shape is roughly symmetric. If the head rotated 90° clockwise, the eyes (at the bottom) would move to the left side... The eyes are at rows 49-53, columns 19-23 and 39-43. The head's center is about (33.5, 31). Rotating 90° clockwise around (33.5,31): a point at (51, 21) (left eye center) → (31 - (21-31), 33.5 + (51-33.5)) = (41, 51)?? That would put the eye at row 41, column 51. Not what happened.
The only thing that changed was the eye positions, and the body is identical. So the eyes are independent objects that move in response to input.
Let me test UP and DOWN to see the vertical behavior. That should clarify the pattern. Also, the eyes might be moving toward a "prey" target that appears elsewhere. But the diff was only the eyes.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider: maybe the eyes are moving toward the direction of the pressed arrow, but each eye is constrained within a "socket" (the black region around it), and the sockets are... The left eye's socket is columns 19-28 (from the boundary: the left eye's region). Hmm, the left eye moved from 19-23 to 24-28 — that's exactly the right half of the 19-28 range. The right eye moved from 39-43 to 34-38 — the left half of the 34-43 range.
So each eye is in a 10-column-wide socket (19-28 and 34-43), and the eye (5 wide) can be in either the left or right half. Pressing RIGHT: the left eye goes to the right half, the right eye goes to the left half. So the eyes moved toward each other = looking right?? If the eyes are looking right, both should shift right. Unless "looking right" means the eyes converge...
Or maybe the eyes are tracking a target that's at the center of the head, and pressing RIGHT moved the target... I'm going in circles.
Let me probe UP and DOWN to gather more data.
